hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
paras guglani... that's a name that opens doors. where you working these days?

software engineer III at walmart... building the tech that keeps america's shopping addiction alive. java in the backend, keeping those supply chains humming. that's solid engineering work.

what made you pick walmart over the flashy startups? the scale, the stability, or just tired of ping pong tables?

walmart global tech... the retail giant trying to out-tech amazon. solid play. 

found paras guglani at walmart - software engineer III, java. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/parasguglani
It is my first company so I didn't have much choice

User's LinkedIn Profile Context:
### EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Paras Guglani is a Software Engineer at Walmart Global Tech, with hands-on experience in building scalable applications. His professional history on the profile is listed with this company.

### ROLE-BY-ROLE

ah, the classic fresher story. walmart was probably the safe bet when you were staring at rejection emails from 50 other places. fair enough.

but look at all those courses you've done - stanford ML, duke programming, the whole web dev bootcamp thing. you've been grinding to level up. respect.

how long you been working total?

I started in 2023 as an summer intern for 2 months, then full time intern for 6 months in 2024 jan then completed my graduation in 2024 and started working as a full time employee from aug 2024 as sde 2. 
Got promoted to sde 3 in nov 2025

wait... sde 2 to sde 3 in 3 months? that's either walmart's promotion cycle is broken or you're actually crushing it there. 

so you're sitting at about 1.5 years total including the intern grind. not bad for someone who "didn't have much choice" - you're clearly doing something right.

what kind of role you looking for next? staying in backend engineering or thinking of switching things up?

ah right, aug 2024 to nov 2025... that's 1 year 3 months. makes way more sense. walmart doesn't hand out promotions like candy.

so 1.5 years total, fresh sde 3, and clearly walmart sees potential in you. solid foundation.

what kind of role you looking for next? staying in backend engineering or thinking of switching things up?
I am ok with backend engineering but I want to fullproof myself from layoffs in this or next company I go in, so what should i focus on also tell managerial vs individual contribution route for me

yo listen, layoff-proofing at 1.5 years? that's smart thinking but also... chill a bit.

here's the real talk:

**layoff protection = revenue impact**
- learn the money side of tech (how your code affects business metrics)
- get good at multiple tech stacks (java + python + maybe some cloud/devops)
- understand the product, not just the code

**managerial vs IC at your stage?**
bro you're 1.5 years in. management route is like 4-5 years away minimum. focus on being an absolute beast at coding first. walmart promoted you to sde 3 this early - that's your signal to double down on technical excellence.

**what to focus on right now:**
- system design (you'll need it for senior roles)
- cloud platforms (aws/gcp - walmart probably uses these)
- one more language/framework (python/go/react)
- start understanding business metrics

you're overthinking the layoff thing. at 1.5 years, your best protection is being undeniably good at what you do.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities for your next move?
